decision.comment:
The reporting stage is mechanically consistent. All cross-referenced numbers check out: confusion-matrix row sums match per-class supports (total 7,180), per-class precision/recall are arithmetically correct (verified for classes 0 and 7), abstain rate 0.411003 × 7,180 = 2,951 matches human_review_count, base_test_accuracy 0.883426 is identical across evaluation_report and abstention_report, and the search report confirms test_metrics_used=false. Schema versions are uniformly 1.0, SHA-256 hashes are present for all blob artefacts, and reporting_status (47 artefact versions, 116 decision events, complete_through_stage=abstention) is coherent.

No deterministic findings were raised. The issues flagged in the evaluation and abstention anomaly reports are model-performance concerns, not reporting-pipeline errors:

1. Val-to-test accuracy gap of ~11.3 pp (99.67 % val vs 88.34 % test) is large and warrants investigation for split-distribution mismatch, but it is correctly reported and does not constitute a reporting defect.
2. OOD AUROC at sigma_0.4 is below 0.5 (0.134 max_softmax, 0.125 predictive_entropy), meaning confidence is anti-correlated with corruption severity at that level. This is a legitimate model limitation, accurately surfaced by the abstention report with ood_pass=false.
3. Validation-to-test coverage gap (~21 pp at the 0.8 target) and risk gap (~80×) indicate the max_softmax threshold does not transfer well; this is a calibration concern, not a reporting error.
4. Class 7 (cancer-associated stroma) recall of 49.4 % is the primary driver of the accuracy shortfall and is correctly reflected in the confusion matrix and per-class table.

All of the above are already captured in the stage anomaly reports with action=revise and severity=warning. The reporting stage faithfully presents these results without omission or misstatement. Because no deterministic finding exists and the reporting artefacts are internally consistent, the appropriate action is to continue with a warning severity to ensure downstream consumers are aware of the performance limitations before any deployment decision.
issues: Val-to-test accuracy gap of ~11.3 pp (99.67 % val vs 88.34 % test) exceeds expected sampling noise; split-distribution mismatch or subtle leakage should be investigated before production use

OOD AUROC at sigma_0.4 is below 0.5 for both max_softmax (0.134) and predictive_entropy (0.125), indicating the abstention mechanism will accept the most corrupted inputs; ood_pass=false is correctly reported
Validation-to-test coverage gap of ~21 pp (0.800 val vs 0.589 test) and risk gap of ~80× (0.000375 val vs 0.030031 test) at the 0.8 target operating point undermine the selective-risk guarantee
Class 7 (cancer-associated stroma) test recall is only 49.4 % (208/421), with 94 misclassified as debris and 75 as smooth muscle; this single class drives most of the accuracy loss

Abstain rate of 41.1 % routes 2,951 test samples to human review, reducing practical selectivity benefit; only max_softmax was used as the abstention score with no ensemble, energy, or Mahalanobis-based alternative evaluated

Early-stopping patience discrepancy (3 in final training vs 5 in search trial) and presence of transformer-specific config fields in the ResNet18 config are noted for reproducibility but do not affect reporting correctness
